To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there is no significant difference in the cyclical response of the real economy to unanticipated monetary shocks between the pre-war and post-1979 regimes; (2) the cyclical response is similar across the pre-war regimes, except for the Great Depression; (3) the cyclical effects are similar across the prewar regimes, except for a higher cyclical response to a contractionary shock in the Great Depression.

(1) the effects of a monetary regime shift on the real economy are not as large as predicted by classical equilibrium models, and (2) the effects of monetary policy on the real economy depend upon the monetary regime.

(a) the effects of monetary shocks on output and prices appear to be similar across regimes; (b) monetary shocks have a significant effect on output in all regimes; and (c) the effect of monetary shocks on prices is significant in some regimes and insignificant in others.
